open_points.subject: Linux host fact used by file-opening modules
open_points.text: “A20 rule 3 ... [is] outside the running kernel ... which no module owns”; however A17 and A18 require “Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`” because “the host is Linux,” while `installation` and `store` have no capability from an owner of that fact.
open_points.question: Who owns the Linux-only host contract on which `installation` and `store` rely, and through what allowed dependency do those modules receive it?
options: Treat Linux support as a release/build invariant that runtime modules may assume directly
Make `data_provider` own and expose the host-platform fact
Give each affected module its own Linux assumption
open_points.default_guess: Treat Linux as a release/build invariant that `installation` and `store` may assume directly.

open_points.subject: Unsupported-host start sequence
open_points.text: A20 says “on any other [host] the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails and the start stops,” but A17 says code uses `O_NOFOLLOW` with “no code asks whether the flag exists,” and State 3 orders `installation.load_installation` and `store.open_store` before `sandbox.probe_sandbox`.
open_points.question: Must every non-Linux start reach and fail the sandbox probe, or may it fail earlier while loading the installation or opening the store because the Linux-only file-opening primitive is unavailable?
options: Non-Linux may fail at the first Linux-specific start operation
The sandbox probe must run before other Linux-specific operations
Installation and store must translate unavailable `O_NOFOLLOW` into the specified sandbox-probe failure
open_points.default_guess: Allow the start to fail at the first Linux-specific operation rather than guaranteeing that the sandbox probe is the failing step.

open_points.subject: SQLite database and journal symlinks created after start
open_points.text: A18 says “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link: the start's walk finds no link before the database is opened,” but also says “A link found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written,” while its invariant remains “symlink_inside(data_directory) -> refused.”
open_points.question: How can `store` guarantee refusal when a database or journal path becomes a symbolic link after the start walk, given that SQLite performs those opens without an available no-follow request, or are those SQLite-managed paths exceptions to the later-link rule and formal invariant?
options: SQLite-managed database and journal paths are exceptions after the start walk
`store` rechecks those paths before every SQLite call despite the remaining check/open race
Use an SQLite opening mechanism that can enforce no-follow semantics
The later-link rule applies only to files opened directly by `store`
open_points.default_guess: Treat SQLite-managed database and journal paths as exceptions after the start walk and narrow the later-link rule and invariant accordingly.
